problem.text: The default EXL3 dispatch reconstructed weights at exactly 32 input rows. The patch moves that boundary so reconstruction begins above 32 rows.

reasoning.text: The threshold counts rows after flattening all leading input dimensions, not just the original batch dimension. Explicit params['reconstruct'] values still override the automatic choice.

impact.text: At exactly 32 flattened rows with no override, forward now uses ext.exl3_gemm instead of allocating and reconstructing a dense inner weight tensor for ext.hgemm. Other row counts retain their previous dispatch.

source_notes.text: The earlier bias-normalization entry describes FP32-to-FP16 constructor conversion; this threshold-only patch leaves that behavior unchanged.

limitations: No CUDA kernel, model inference or repository test was executed; numerical equivalence and performance gains remain unmeasured.
The inspected evidence establishes the boundary change but not why 32 is the preferred crossover.

chapters.title: Keep 32-row EXL3 operations on the quantized path

claims.text: Both branches first apply the input Hadamard transform. Reconstruction obtains a fresh half-precision matrix shaped (in_features, out_features), fills it through ext.reconstruct, and passes it to ext.hgemm. The alternative passes the packed trellis directly to ext.exl3_gemm. Output transforms, bias addition and output dtype handling are unchanged.

A standard-library transcription checked row counts 1–4096: only 32 changed its default branch. Explicit True and False overrides remained unchanged at sampled boundary-adjacent sizes. This checks dispatch arithmetic, not tensor execution.

The existing test_qgemm includes sizes 31, 32 and 33 and compares explicitly forced quantized and reconstructed outputs. Because both calls supply reconstruct, that test does not exercise the changed automatic threshold.

annotation.summary: Changes automatic EXL3 reconstruction from at least 32 flattened input rows to more than 32, preserving explicit overrides.
